Rust programming language

Rust is a systems programming language focused on safety, speed, and concurrency. It gives developers control over memory without requiring a garbage collector.

Ownership and borrowing prevent common data races while expressive types document intent.

The language is used for command line tools, network services, embedded software, and browser components.

API Reference Guide Examples

fn fetch(url: &str) -> Result<Response>

The client validates the URL and returns a bounded response with status, headers, and body.

Error handling

Callers receive an explicit timeout, invalid request, or transport error and can retry only safe operations.

Examples use deterministic local fixtures so documentation remains useful while offline.

Build notes for a small personal browser

A personal browser can stay responsive by bounding network responses, runtime work, decoded media, and caches.

Measurements guide each optimization: a fast test loop catches local mistakes, while a release tier checks high-risk integration paths.

Memory pressure first evicts stale cache entries, then sleeps inactive tabs, and only discards eligible tabs as a last resort.
